anti_overlap: Does not assess whether the adapter adds sufficient value — only whether the spec's requirements are normatively precise and independently testable
Does not assess brand or naming rights — only the structural precision of conformance criteria
Does not review the promotion ladder stages for artifact lifecycle — only whether conformance thresholds for the adapter name itself are measurable
decision_lens: Can an independent implementer read this spec and produce a conformant Athenflux without consulting the authors? Which clauses are normative and which are illustrative? Is there a conformance test surface?
distance_rationale: Standards body practice is a professional discipline with established doctrine on protocol vs implementation separation, normative language, conformance classes, and testability. IETF RFC methodology and W3C conformance levels directly map to the challenge of specifying what an adapter must inherit unchanged vs may add, and whether the specification can generate independent implementations.
expected_isomorphisms: IETF MUST/SHOULD/MAY vocabulary maps to the adapter spec's need to distinguish binding inheritance obligations from optional extensions
W3C conformance class definitions (A/AA/AAA or feature-based) map to whether Athenflux minimum qualification admits partial conformance
Protocol vs implementation separation in IETF RFCs maps to interflux (protocol) vs Athenflux (implementation layer) separation
focus: Standards body conformance discipline: separation of protocol specification from implementation, how conformance is defined and tested, and whether the adapter spec provides a testable conformance surface rather than aspirational description.
name: fd-standards-conformance
persona: Apply the perspective of a standards body working group editor (W3C, IETF, or ISO) — they care about normative vs informative distinctions, measurable conformance requirements, and whether a specification can generate independent interoperable implementations.
review_areas: Normative vs informative separation: whether the spec distinguishes binding requirements from examples, guidance, and rationale using standard vocabulary (MUST/SHOULD/MAY or equivalent)
Conformance class definition: whether the spec defines what a conformant implementation is, what a non-conformant one is, and whether partial conformance is recognized
Interoperability scope: whether the boundary between inherited interflux behavior and Athenflux-added behavior is precise enough for a second independent implementer to reproduce correctly
Testability of qualification rule: whether the four minimum conditions in the qualification rule can be verified by inspection or test, or require author judgment
Version coupling: whether the spec addresses how Athenflux conformance should be declared against a specific interflux version, and what happens when upstream revises the inherited contract

severity_examples.condition: The entire spec uses 'should' uniformly, making it impossible to determine which requirements are binding vs advisory — a conformant and a non-conformant implementation would look identical against the spec
The spec defines minimum conditions for earning the name but does not define what a compliant vs non-compliant implementation is, leaving no way to assess conformance without author judgment
The spec does not state which version of interflux the inherited contract is drawn from, meaning upstream revisions may silently invalidate declared conformance without any detection mechanism

success_hints: Binding requirements are clearly marked with 'must' or normative equivalents, informative sections are labeled as such
Qualification rule conditions are independently verifiable without author interpretation
The inherited contract is anchored to a specific upstream version or version range
A second implementation could claim conformance by demonstrating the same four minimum conditions
task_context: An adapter boundary specification that defines what a host-specific operational layer must inherit unchanged, what it may add, and when it qualifies to carry its own name — reviewed for whether the spec is precise enough to generate independent interoperable implementations.
